purpose: Every deliberate move of a §8.9.19 FRAME WITNESS (`source_digest`, `toolchain`) in evidence/proof_ledger.jsonl, with an owner and a reason. Read ci/check_ledger_census.py for the argument; the short form is that on 2026-08-04 an author regenerating the ledger from a base that predated a re-witness put the withdrawn digests back on 115 of 121 entries, and NOTHING SAW IT: no key went missing, so the key census and the loss invariant both reported 0, and on Windows a stale source digest with matching SPIR-V is SOURCE-COSMETIC, which forgives, so `--check` printed PASS over all 115. Only the Linux lane declined, and it declined 115 entries and the op suite with them. A witness move is legitimate and routine; a witness move NOBODY WROTE DOWN is indistinguishable from that accident.
why_not_a_value_rule: The first version of this arm asked 'did the value go back to something a later revision replaced'. That question is SYMMETRIC: it convicted the repair exactly as loudly as it convicted the regression, because from the values alone the two are the same event seen from opposite ends. A screen cannot rank two alternating values without a frame, and the ledger records no frame for its own hashing rule. So the question asked is not 'which value is right' — it is 'did the writer say they were moving it', which has an answer in the repository and needs no build, no device and no second platform.
how_to_add_a_record: One record per (revision, field). `revision` is the commit that carries the move, or the literal WORKTREE for an uncommitted one — WORKTREE records must be re-pointed at the real sha before merge, and a WORKTREE record that matches nothing fails as `stale_rewitness_declaration`. BECAUSE THIS REPOSITORY SQUASH-MERGES, a sha written while the work is on a branch is ALSO temporary: the squash mints a new commit and the branch commit never becomes an ancestor of main, so a record left pointing at it names a revision the repository does not contain. Re-point branch shas at the MERGE commit in a follow-up, exactly as for WORKTREE. Say WHY the witness moved: `--reprove` (the kernel changed) and `--backfill-frame --rewitness-source` (the source text or the hashing rule changed while the SPIR-V is byte-identical, which is the evidence the subject did not) are different events and only the second is a re-witness.
screened_since_note: The merge that first carried a portable source_digest into main. Moves in revisions that are not descendants of it predate the rule this screen enforces and are counted and named, not failed — the same append-only discipline as `retired` in ci/open_reds.json. Adopting a screen must not retroactively convict history it could not have governed.

rewitness.reason: NOT a re-witness — an accident, recorded because it happened and not to excuse it. The Conv commit regenerated evidence/proof_ledger.jsonl from a base predating aea0147 and restored the digests computed under the WITHDRAWN pre-`normalize_shader_text` rule on 115 of 121 entries. Every existing screen read clean: no key went missing (key census 0 VANISHED, loss invariant 0 missing) and Windows `--check` printed PASS because a stale source digest with matching SPIR-V is SOURCE-COSMETIC, which forgives. Linux read the same 115 as SUBJECT-CHANGED and declined; the op suite went 8 failed to 50 failed, the criterion-10 gate to UNATTRIBUTED, epctl --check-counters to exit 3 and the portability screen to claimed_nothing. Repaired in the 69ac222 record above. This arm is the screen that would have caught it at the merge.
rewitness.how_this_gets_closed: It does not get deleted. The same argument as `retired` in ci/open_reds.json: deleting the record removes the CHECK's memory of the event, not the event. It stays with deliberate=false so the next reader can see that this class of accident has happened once and what it cost.

rewitness.reason: Re-running the re-witness that aea0147 landed and eee65aa undid. eee65aa regenerated the ledger from a base predating aea0147, restoring the digests computed under the WITHDRAWN pre-`normalize_shader_text` rule on 115 of 121 entries; the 6 survivors are the entries that commit newly proved (Conv x4, Add f32, Clip f32), which carry a current digest by construction. Windows read the result as 121 entries = 6 identical + 115 SOURCE-COSMETIC and printed PASS; Linux read the same file as 6 PROVEN-ELSEWHERE{toolchain} + 115 SUBJECT-CHANGED and declined, taking the op suite from 8 failed to 50. After the re-witness Windows reads 121 identical.

rewitness.owner_attribution: DERIVED, not claimed by the author. Every commit in this repository is authored by justinchuby; the owner recorded here is read off the commits subject and the paths it touched (counters.rs plus a wholesale rewrite of bench/results counter artifacts, which is Mouses lane). If mouse says otherwise this field is wrong and should be corrected rather than deleted.
rewitness.reason: The SECOND firing of the eee65aa accident, same shape, smaller count, and it went unseen for the same reason: the ledger write rode along inside a commit about something else. A counters commit regenerated evidence/proof_ledger.jsonl from a base predating the 69ac222 re-witness and put the withdrawn pre-normalize_shader_text source_digest back on 13 entries. No key moved, so the key census and the loss invariant both read 0; Windows --check forgives a stale source digest whose SPIR-V still matches as SOURCE-COSMETIC. Recorded because it happened, not to excuse it: this arm is the only screen in the repository that can see a field move inside a surviving entry.

The repair of 18ddece, declared late: the commit landed on main before this register was consulted, which is itself the finding — a re-witness that is correct and undeclared is indistinguishable to this screen from the accident it repairs, and the screen said so by convicting both. 9 and not 13 because four of the thirteen keys were retired by Morpheus 8.9.23 between the accident and the repair and are now in evidence/retired_proof_keys.json; the surviving nine carry d29f419bfe2c97ee, the digest computed under the current normalize_shader_text rule, which is what the ledger reads today.

NOT a re-witness in the sense this register was built for — the hashing rule did not move, the KERNEL did. Issue #4 replaced GLSL's `asin()`/`acos()` in rust/shaders/glsl/templates/ew_unary.comp with a portable minimax core (`ew_asin_core`/`ew_asin_abs`/`ew_asin`/`ew_acos`), because Vulkan defines both built-ins by inheritance from `atan2`, which is allowed 4096 ULP in single precision; lavapipe measured 3831/3903 ULP against the ORT CPU EP and was conformant while missing FP32_TRANSCENDENTAL by 15x. Different source and different SPIR-V means a different subject, so the two entries had to be re-proved rather than re-witnessed: without the reprove the EP correctly read both as SUBJECT-CHANGED and declined them, which is the negative control working. Re-proved on NVIDIA RTX A1000, verdict MATCH, worst_rel 1.79e-07 (Acos) with dispatches_executed=1. Declared here because the screen cannot tell a deliberate kernel change from a regeneration off a stale base by looking at the digests alone — only the writer can say which happened.
rewitness.how_this_gets_closed: It does not get deleted. `revision` was WORKTREE while the change was uncommitted, was re-pointed at 601ddcf on squad/4-portable-inverse-trig, and was re-pointed AGAIN at e3d3cf6 here (issue #43) because PR #35 landed as a SQUASH merge: the squash minted a new commit for the whole branch and 601ddcf is not an ancestor of main, so the declaration named a revision this repository no longer contains and ci/check_ledger_census.py read it as `stale_rewitness_declaration` while reading the identical move under e3d3cf6 as `undeclared_witness_move`. Both arms were describing ONE event from two sides. The lesson generalises past this record: under a squash-merge workflow, any `revision` in this register that names a branch commit is live only until the PR merges, so a record written on a branch MUST be re-pointed at the merge commit — the same discipline `how_to_add_a_record` already states for WORKTREE, for the same reason and with one more step.

rewitness.reason: The OTHER half of e3d3cf6, and the cause of issue #43. `source_digest_for` hashes the WHOLE text of a template plus its includes, so per-variant uniqueness comes from STEM + VARIANT-DEFINE + ARGV and not from preprocessing. rust/shaders/glsl/templates/ew_unary.comp is shared by 42 op selectors, so #35's edits to it — the Cephes attribution header and the new ew_asin_core/ew_asin_abs/ew_asin/ew_acos functions, which only Asin and Acos ever call — moved the source_digest of ALL 55 ew_unary-derived entries at once, not just the 2 that changed kernel. #35 re-proved those 2 and left the other 53 carrying a digest computed from source text that no longer exists. NOTHING SAW IT, for the third time and by the third distinct route: the census arm above sees only values that MOVE IN THE FILE and these never moved in the file, they went stale under it; and on Windows a stale source_digest whose SPIR-V still matches is SOURCE-COSMETIC, which forgives, so --check printed PASS over all 55. Linux convicted 5 of them — IsInf@sel1/sel2/sel3, IsNaN and Not — because CI's shaderc emits different SPIR-V for exactly those five, and once BOTH witnesses have moved the checker cannot tell a moved compiler from a moved kernel and must decline. The EP declining is the negative control WORKING; test_op_table[IsInf|IsNaN|Not] failed at assert_vulkan_claims, with correct numerics throughout. Re-witnessed and not re-proved because the subject demonstrably did not change: --backfill-frame refuses per entry unless the recorded spirv_digest AND toolchain both match this build's, and all 55 passed that guard (55 re-witnessed, 0 skipped), which is the evidence. Re-proving would have been the wrong instrument twice over — it asserts a kernel change that did not happen, and it would have rewritten 55 canonical `device` frames from the ledger's NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU to this machine's NVIDIA RTX A1000. The diff is 55 source_digest fields and nothing else: no key added, none removed, no spirv_digest and no device touched. Windows --check goes 78 identical + 55 SOURCE-COSMETIC to 133 identical.
rewitness.how_this_gets_closed: It does not get deleted. `revision` was WORKTREE while the change was uncommitted and now names 0b56195, the branch commit that carries the move. IF PR #43 IS SQUASH-MERGED THIS RECORD MUST BE RE-POINTED AT THE SQUASH COMMIT IN AN IMMEDIATE FOLLOW-UP, because 0b56195 will not be an ancestor of main and this register will then name a revision the repository does not contain — which is exactly the `undeclared_witness_move` + `stale_rewitness_declaration` pair this commit is fixing for e3d3cf6. A normal merge commit needs no follow-up, because the branch commit stays reachable. This is a KNOWN GAP in the screen and not a slip: a declaration must be written before the merge exists, so under squash-merge no record can ever name its own landing commit, and the register is structurally one commit behind. Fixing that properly means letting a record name something stable across a squash and is a change to ci/check_ledger_census.py's matching rule, which is Morpheus's ruling to make (§8.9.19) and deliberately not made here. Until it is, the follow-up re-point is the process, and `how_to_add_a_record` says so.
rewitness.standing_repair: tests/ops/test_proof_ledger.py::test_no_entry_carries_a_stale_source_digest, added with this record. It compares every recorded source_digest against the one this build computes and fails on a mismatch WITHOUT consulting SPIR-V, so it is platform-independent and would have failed on the author's own Windows machine the moment #35 touched the shared template. Both pre-existing screens are blind to a stale-but-unmoved witness — the census sees only values that move in the file, and --check forgives a stale source digest whose SPIR-V still matches. That test is the one that is not blind, and tests/ops/test_unary_boundary.py is the collateral-damage control on what the shared ops COMPUTE.
